description: A district director of assessment must certify the resolution plan after an answer-review screen was briefly visible during a middle-school mathematics assessment session, including score handling, retesting, family notification, and record retention, with input from the school testing coordinator, principal, multilingual learner coordinator, and information-security analyst.

shared_context.S1: During one middle-school mathematics assessment session, an answer-review screen was visible to students for part of the testing period.
shared_context.S2: The district director of assessment must certify the incident resolution plan before score reports are released.
shared_context.S3: The draft plan proposes canceling the entire session, giving all students an online retest, sending one English notice to families, and retaining the incident records for 90 days.
shared_context.S4: The district's incident-review routine includes a check-in with the school testing coordinator, principal, multilingual learner coordinator, and information-security analyst before certification.

PF1.text: The completed seating chart and proctor statement identify exactly six students who could see the answer-review screen. The state incident protocol requires invalidating only those six students' scores and offering their retest within 10 school days; Ms. Shah completed this reconciliation yesterday, but the result has not been entered in the district incident tracker.

PF2.text: One of the six affected students has an approved assessment accommodation requiring a paper test rather than an online retest. Mr. Ortiz confirmed the accommodation in the student's current plan this morning, but has not yet attached it to the incident record.

PF3.text: The affected students' family-contact records show that the required incident notice must be issued in English, Spanish, and Somali. Ms. Hassan verified the language preferences with families this week, but the notice template still lists English only.

PF4.text: The district security schedule requires assessment-incident evidence, including access logs and proctor statements, to be retained for exactly 180 days. Mr. Nguyen confirmed this requirement against the current security-retention schedule yesterday, but the draft plan still says 90 days.

acceptance_conditions: Only the six affected students' scores must be invalidated.
Exactly six students must be identified as affected.
The affected students must be offered a paper retest.
The retest must occur within exactly 10 school days.
Family notices must be issued in English, Spanish, and Somali.
Incident evidence must be retained for exactly 180 days.
A formal retest-and-score-resolution commitment must be recorded.
A formal multilingual-notice commitment must be recorded.
A formal evidence-retention commitment must be recorded.

decisive_facts.why: The seating-chart reconciliation changes the affected scope from the draft's entire session to exactly six students and sets their retest deadline at exactly 10 school days.
The approved accommodation changes the retest mode for the affected group from the draft's online test to a paper test.
The verified family preferences change the notice language set from English only to exactly English, Spanish, and Somali and require the multilingual-notice commitment.
The current security-retention schedule changes the evidence period from the draft's 90 days to exactly 180 days and requires the assessment-evidence-retention commitment.
